messages.author: 6f17ff4d1bfe11d7
messages.subject: Distribution
parts:
Hi,

I am working with species data.  exponential or Weibull for variables with ranges that extend above one. Not sure about the [0,1] variables. Beta distributions tend not to have spikes at both 0 and 1. This is usually described as a bathtub distribution. 

I have a diversity measure lay between [0,1]. Any ideas I can do with R-INLA?

Thanks in advance.

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Distribution
parts:
the only option for continous response in the interval (0,1) is the Beta
distribution.

if you have censored variables that lives on [0,infty> but is either
censored or observed in [0,1], that is doable as well using
'inla.surv()'
